exposure: frequent prenatal surveillance (>= once weekly fetal well-being testing)
cohort: The study included 61 actively treated pregnancies with high-risk fetal heart disease from 2006-2020 at a single center.
finding: Abnormal fetal surveillance results and/or a CVPS ≤7 may identify compromised fetuses with high-risk fetal heart disease who are at higher risk of mortality and could benefit from altered management or expedited delivery.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean delivery was significantly more common in cases where fetal surveillance results were abnormal.
